summary: Pause no longer kills autoplay: the voice-death monitor misread an intentional pause as a dead connection and tore the session down with zero notification.
details: The death monitor (voice_session.py) probes every 5s: a track is loaded AND `is_playing()==False` for two consecutive ticks means 'dead'. `pause()` clears discord.py's `AudioPlayer._resumed`, so `is_playing()` returns False for the whole pause — a paused track tripped the false-positive death path after ~10s. Found live 2026-09-15: pause clicked 13:30:21, monitor declared the connection dead 13:30:30, both reconnect attempts failed with `discord.ClientException: Already connected to a voice channel.` (the connection was ALIVE — `guild.voice_client` still held the channel), and the session was torn down. The room heard nothing.
Fix 1 — `DiscordVoiceSession` tracks `_paused`; the monitor treats an intentional pause as healthy and resets its dead-tick counter. `pause()`/`resume()` set it.

Fix 2 — `_try_reconnect` recognises `Already connected to a voice channel.` as PROOF the connection is alive (a false-positive death probe), logs it and keeps the session rather than signalling death. This is the belt-and-braces path for any future false positive.

Fix 3 — `MusicPlayerManager._leave(..., announce=True)` announces the teardown with `connection_lost_line()` ('Music stopped — voice connection lost. Use /music play to restart.'). Only the voice-death path passes `announce=True`; `/music stop` already replies `Stopped.` and idle timeouts are expected silence, so they do not double-post. Announcement is idempotent — a second `_leave` on an already-torn guild has no player and stays silent.

Tests: the fake voice client now reproduces real discord.py pause semantics (`is_playing()` False while paused, `_resumed` cleared/set), three new session tests (monitor silent while paused and re-armed after resume; reconnect survives an 'Already connected' false-positive) and three new manager tests (voice-death leave announces; plain leave stays silent; no double-post).
limitations: The announce line is only as good as the notify closure — a session whose originating channel is no longer messageable logs a warning and drops it, matching the existing now-playing path.

A REAL voice death that happens while paused is not detected until someone resumes — the monitor intentionally skips pause. That matches user expectation (paused = intentionally silent) at the cost of not noticing a connection drop mid-pause.
